genreClassification.rationale: The song is a foundational track in alternative/nu-metal, matching the heavy, detuned tone profile.

Ollama.targetTone: Dark, heavily saturated, mid-scooped sludge tone with massive sustain and controlled feedback.
gearHypotheses: High-gain Tube Screamer style overdrive (for grit) -> Fuzz pedal (for sludge)
Amp simulation with Marshall or Mesa Boogie character

finalVerdict.targetTone: thick detuned nu-metal crunch with tight low end and cold chorus space
corrections: swap sludge fuzz for tight modern hi-gain
avoid mid-scoop as the main cue

gp180.choicePolicy: Focus on modern, tight hi-gain tones suitable for dropped tuning and nu-metal crunch.
gp180.bestMatchSummary: A high-gain signal chain utilizing a Distortion/Fuzz stage followed by the Recti amp model into a 4x12 cab, complemented by Chorus and Gate effects to achieve thick, detuned, and tight modern rock tones.

blocks.purpose: Tighten the low end and eliminate hum inherent in heavy chugging.
blocks.gap: None

blocks.purpose: Provide initial saturation and tighten the attack for palm-muted chugs.
blocks.gap: Using Boost as a general drive enhancer, simulating an overdrive boost before the main distortion stage.

alternatives.reason: If more grit is needed early in the chain.

blocks.purpose: Establish the core thick hi-gain wall required for nu-metal crunch and dropped tuning.
blocks.gap: The 'Distortion' model is chosen over specific fuzz/overdrive models to capture the modern, tight saturation of Mesa/modern high-gain amps.

alternatives.reason: If a more aggressive, mid-focused crunch is desired.

blocks.purpose: Kept inactive to maintain maximum low-end punch and avoid unnecessary filtering.
blocks.gap: The target tone does not require a wah effect; this slot is reserved for potential future use or bypassed entirely.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the modern, tight, high-gain character of a Mesa/modern amp setup.
blocks.gap: The Recti model is the best fit for heavy, scooped, yet defined low-end tones typical of nu-metal and dropped tuning.

alternatives.reason: If a slightly more British/hard rock flavor was desired.

blocks.purpose: Provide a robust and full-bodied cabinet sound suitable for heavy rhythm playing.
blocks.gap: The Mess 4x12 offers a versatile, modern voicing that complements the tight low end of the Recti model.

alternatives.reason: If a slightly more classic rock tone was preferred.

blocks.purpose: Add the required subtle chorus space without creating a dominant wash.
blocks.gap: Settings are dialed back to ensure subtlety, matching the 'slight chorus' requirement and avoiding excessive modulation.

alternatives.reason: If a rhythmic pulsing effect was needed instead of space.

blocks.purpose: Provide minimal, natural room ambience to give depth without the 'big reverb wash' warned against.
blocks.gap: The mix and decay time are kept low to ensure the effect is supportive rather than dominant.

alternatives.reason: If a more controlled, metallic ambience was desired.

blocks.purpose: Disabled to avoid excessive wash and maintain the tight, aggressive focus of the rhythm tone.
blocks.gap: The 'corrections' explicitly state dropping heavy delay/reverb wash; thus, this module is bypassed.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment.
blocks.gap: Standard final stage control.

warnings: The source material is a modern rock/nu-metal track, requiring a focus on tight, aggressive hi-gain tones rather than classic rock or clean sounds.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the modern, thick, and defined low end required for nu-metal chugging.

proposals.reason: The current IR may lack the necessary tightness and low-end definition for dropped tuning chugs.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased punch and clarity in the low end.
